comments.content: JSON built via `format!` with direct interpolation of `new` content. If any corpus content contained `"`, `\`, `{`, or `}`, the resulting JSON would be malformed. Currently safe for the hardcoded corpus, but fragile to future test data additions or copy-paste edits. Consider building a structured value (e.g. `serde_json::json!`) and stringifying it for stronger guarantees.

The assertion loop calls `store::load_all(&conn)` once per corpus item (10 times total), full-scanning the shared test database each iteration. Since every pipeline run finishes before the assertion loop starts, a single `load_all` outside the loop plus an in-memory `filter` would cut this from O(n×m) to O(n+m). Not a correctness bug, but the shared test DB already accumulates rows from sibling tests, so the cost compounds.

`client` and `base_url` are cloned twice per iteration: once in the loop body to feed the outer `move`, then again inside the closure's `async move` block. The outer clones are sufficient — the inner ones are redundant. Hoist the `base_url` clone and pass `client` / `base_url` straight into the `async move` to simplify the closure.

In the not-found branch of `model_get`, the literal sets `provider_key: None` explicitly, but the immediately following `**provider_fallback("?")` spread carries `provider_key: "?"` and silently overrides it (Python keeps the last value when keys collide in a literal/spread). The explicit `None` is dead code — the actual returned value is `"?"`. This is semantically misleading: any consumer that distinguishes "model missing" via `response.provider_key is None` will mis-classify the fallback as "model associated with a provider named '?'", while another consumer inspecting the `source` field will reach the opposite conclusion. The intent of the fallback (placeholder `"?"` vs `None`) is now ambiguous. Decide which semantics is intended and make the literal match — e.g. drop the `provider_key: None` line if `"?"` is the intended placeholder, or drop the `provider_fallback("?")` spread (and inline only the genuinely-needed provider fields) if `None` is the intended sentinel.

`model_upsert` returns `{"ok": False, "error": "..."}` with HTTP 200 status when the referenced `provider_key` does not exist, instead of raising `HTTPException(status_code=..., detail=...)`. This deviates from FastAPI conventions: clients must inspect the response body for an `ok` flag rather than relying on the HTTP status code. The same non-idiomatic shape is also used in `sync_now` (success and failure both return 200 with `{"ok": ...}`), reinforcing the asymmetry vs. all the read endpoints which use the standard FastAPI return-shape. Prefer raising `HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=f"provider 不存在: {body.provider_key}，请先 POST /api/provider")` so the error is visible in the status code and tooling (Swagger, logs, proxies) handles it correctly.
comments.existing_code:
if not conn.execute("SELECT 1 FROM provider WHERE provider_key=?", (body.provider_key,)).fetchone():
            return {"ok": False, "error": f"provider 不存在: {body.provider_key}，请先 POST /api/provider"}

comments.content: `httpx.get(MODELS_DEV_API, timeout=10)` in `sync_models_dev` does not use a response context manager, so the underlying connection is only released on garbage collection. For the one-shot lifespan call this is harmless, but `/api/sync-models-dev` re-invokes `sync_models_dev` on demand and can be triggered repeatedly; over time the default client's connection pool may accumulate idle connections that are not cleanly returned. Prefer `with httpx.Client(timeout=10) as client: data = client.get(MODELS_DEV_API).json()` so the response is closed deterministically.

断言「裁决请求里应含候选记忆清单」实现为对 `bodies` 全量 `any`，未限定为裁决请求。若抽取 prompt 后续误增类似文本（如扩写「已有记忆」示例），该 sanity 会假阳性通过、掩盖 build_adjudication_msgs 实际断线。建议按调用顺序只检查裁决请求（bodies[1], bodies[3], …）——也是「Confirm 档 now 统一」之后定位「哪一档 prompt 缺候选清单」唯一可靠的索引。

「抽取+裁决 各一次 = 2×corpus.len()」硬编码与 `Confirm 档 now 统一` 的方向冲突——一旦确认档合并入抽取 prompt、或裁决前增一次重排/校验 LLM 调用，本测试会立刻红，但实际语义并未退化；断言信息「实得 N」只报数字、不区分是「多了 1 抽」还是「多了 1 确认」。建议拆成两步：① 断言「至少每组 ≥2 次」+ `request_bodies()` 中裁决请求数 ≥corpus.len()，把「每组恰好 2 次」的脆弱性下沉到 pipeline 自己的单测。

The PALETTE color assignment via `hash(pkey)` does not match the "稳定" (stable) claim in the comment above the PALETTE list. Python's `hash()` for strings uses SipHash with a per-process random seed (PYTHONHASHSEED), so the same provider_key would receive different fallback colors on different process restarts and on any fresh database — i.e. across deployments of this metadata service. Since this assignment runs only inside `sync_models_dev` and the column is written on INSERT (the ON CONFLICT branch does not re-write `fallback_color`), this means each fresh DB / first-time sync ends up with a different palette mapping, contradicting the stated intent. Use a deterministic hash such as `zlib.crc32(pkey.encode()) % len(PALETTE)` or `int.from_bytes(hashlib.blake2b(pkey.encode(), digest_size=4).digest(), 'big') % len(PALETTE)` to get true cross-deployment stability.
